description: Table 1 is a plain three-column text table (no plots or images) whose column heads are "Descriptor", "Formula" and "Ref.", with six data rows defining the machine-learning input features. Row 1: "valence electron concentration (VEC)", VEC = Σ_{i=1}^{n} c_i VEC_i, Ref. [32]. Row 2: "melting point (Tm)", ΔT_m = Σ_{i=1}^{n} c_i T_mi, Ref. [33]. Row 3: "entropy of mixing (ΔSmix)", ΔS_mix = −R Σ_{i=1}^{n} c_i ln(c_i), Ref. [32]. Row 4: "enthalpy of mixing (ΔHmix)", ΔH_mix = 4 Σ_{i≠j}^{n} c_i c_j H_ij, Ref. [34]. Row 5: "Pauli electronegativity difference (Δχ)", printed as χ̄ = Σ_{i=1}^{n} c_i r_i together with Δχ = √(Σ_{i=1}^{n} c_i (χ̄ − χ_i)²), Ref. [35]. Row 6: "atomic size difference (δ)", δ = √(Σ_{i=1}^{n} Σ_{j>i}^{n} c_i c_j (1 − (r_i + r_j)/(2r̄))²), Ref. [36]. All formulas are set in italic serif math type and are fully legible; symbols are not separately defined in the table (c_i appears as element fraction, r_i atomic radius, n the number of components). No numeric values, units, samples or conditions are printed anywhere in the table. The caption states these are the "Original six input features used in machine learning model"; the citing text adds that they were selected to improve model accuracy for the (100-x-y-z)Fe-xMn-yAl-zC system.

observations.observation: The table has exactly three columns headed 'Descriptor', 'Formula' and 'Ref.' and contains six data rows.
Row 1 gives the descriptor 'valence electron concentration (VEC)' with the formula VEC = Σ_{i=1}^{n} c_i VEC_i and reference [32].
Row 2 gives 'melting point (Tm)' with the formula printed as ΔT_m = Σ_{i=1}^{n} c_i T_mi and reference [33].
Row 3 gives 'entropy of mixing (ΔSmix)' with the formula ΔS_mix = −R Σ_{i=1}^{n} c_i ln(c_i) and reference [32].
Row 4 gives 'enthalpy of mixing (ΔHmix)' with the formula ΔH_mix = 4 Σ_{i≠j}^{n} c_i c_j H_ij and reference [34].
Row 5 gives 'Pauli electronegativity difference (Δχ)'; the first printed expression is χ̄ = Σ_{i=1}^{n} c_i r_i and the second is Δχ = √(Σ_{i=1}^{n} c_i (χ̄ − χ_i)²), with reference [35].
Row 6 gives 'atomic size difference (δ)' with the formula δ = √(Σ_{i=1}^{n} Σ_{j>i}^{n} c_i c_j (1 − (r_i + r_j)/(2r̄))²) and reference [36].
The reference column cites [32], [33], [34], [35] and [36], with [32] used twice (for VEC and for ΔSmix).
The table prints no numeric values, no units and no sample or processing-condition labels; only symbols and formulas appear.
The caption states the table lists the 'Original six input features used in machine learning model'.

The citing text states the six selected descriptors are VEC, atomic size difference (δ), enthalpy of mixing (ΔHmix), entropy of mixing (ΔSmix), melting point (Tm) and Pauli electronegativity difference (Δχ), chosen to improve the accuracy of the machine-learning models.
The citing text states the descriptor selection was made for the (100-x-y-z)Fe-xMn-yAl-zC low-density austenitic steel family with 10% ≤ x ≤ 30%, 2% ≤ y ≤ 12% and 0.2% ≤ z ≤ 2% (mass percentage).
